business_scope.primary_industry_name: Bonded Warehouse Wholesale Trade of Aged Scotch and Bordeaux Wines

Convention between the Government of the Republic of Korea and the Government of the People's Republic of China for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with respect to Taxes on Income (1994)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Using Specified Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 6516, as amended) and its Enforcement Decree; Act on Real Name Financial Transactions and Guarantee of Confidentiality (Act No. 18970, as amended); Commercial Act, Articles 287-2 through 287-40; Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and Enforcement Decree; KoFIU examination rules and Financial Services Commission regulations on customer due diligence and beneficial owner identification.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Certificate of Registered Matters and Business Registration Certificate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: District Court Registration Office and National Tax Service
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Issue original registry extract/tax business certificate -> notarize by Korean notary public if required -> obtain Hague Apostille from Republic of Korea Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA). Consular legalization is not used because Korea is a Hague Apostille Convention member; the Apostille and consular paths are mutually exclusive and never chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Tax Clearance Certificate and Corporate Registry Existence Certificate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National Tax Service and District Court Registration Office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Obtain tax clearance certificate from jurisdictional tax office and current corporate registry certificate -> notarize if required -> MOFA Apostille; no consular legalization route for Apostille-member recipients.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution Authorizing Representative Director and Power of Attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of KR_YUHANGHOESA, countersigned by Korean notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified copy of board minutes and executed power of attorney -> notarization -> MOFA Apostille; must not be subsequently submitted to consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (Notarized Statutory Deed of Incorporation)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Incorporators of KR_YUHANGHOESA and Korean notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Draft and execute articles -> notarization by Korean notary -> MOFA Apostille. The Apostille is the exclusive authentication method in all member states.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Qualified Korean commercial bank (upon account opening)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank branch letter with authorized bank officer signature -> notarization of signature -> MOFA Apostille; consular legalization is not appended and cannot be combined.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence screens must be run for every UBO, director, officer, shareholder, authorized signatory and material counterparty against the Korean Ministry of Economy and Finance financial sanctions list, the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs designated-persons list, the OFAC SDN list, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU and UK sanctions lists, and global PEP databases. For foreign PEPs, domestic prominent public officials, and their family/close associates, independent source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification is required. Bonded spirits and wine transactions with high-risk jurisdictions, cash settlements, third-party payments, or rapid transshipment patterns require enhanced transaction monitoring, negative news/reputational screening, and annual rescreening updates.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (iROS) company-name search portal and Korean Courts Electronic Registration System
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Commercial Act Article 19 requires trade names to be written in the Korean script; Latin alphabet words and Arabic numerals may be used only as supplementary signs, and any foreign term must be phonetically transliterated into Korean. The legal-form suffix must be 'Yuhan Hoesa' (LLC designator). The four-tier naming sequence is: (1) distinctive coined element, (2) business-object descriptor, (3) legal-form suffix, and (4) optional registered-business identifier for the bonded spirits and wine wholesale activity.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant should submit a written re-examination request to the same registry court within seven days, attaching comparative evidence of dissimilarity or a ministerial approval letter. If re-examination fails, an administrative appeal may be filed in the competent district court under the Administrative Litigation Act within ninety days, and a constitutional complaint is available for due-process violations. In parallel, counsel should immediately file an alternative name with a new distinctive element to freeze the reservation timeline and preserve the commercial closing schedule.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For a bonded-warehouse wholesaler of aged Scotch and Bordeaux wines, a virtual office or commercial mailbox is not permissible as the sole registered office or principal place of business. The Liquor Tax Act, Customs Act and National Tax Service place-of-business registration require a physical commercial address with actual operational substance, an approved bonded warehouse, and inventory storage. Banks reject virtual-office accounts and require an on-site visit and photo verification. A registered-agent address may supplement, but cannot replace, the physical operating office that must be established before licensing.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High. Quantified risk: approximately 80% probability of an unannounced on-site inspection by the National Tax Service, district customs office or municipal licensing authority within the first twelve months. Required verification checklist: current lease agreement and paid rent receipts, landlord identification and property deed evidence, physical office signage and employee presence, approved bonded warehouse and customs bond, stock ledgers and liquor tax stamp records, sales invoices, and the corporate seal/tax invoice system linked to the registered address.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No official name-search fee; attorney time billed separately at prevailing market rates.

Court Fees Act schedule for corporation registration applications.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notary Fee Act statutory schedule, approximating KRW 70,000-90,000 for standard LLC formation documents.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille fee for each document bundle (5 instruments)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: MOFA Apostille fee schedule per certificate, with prevailing market service charge if processed through a courier.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Outside corporate counsel and AML compliance adviser
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for a standard Korean Yuhan Hoesa formation and AML/CFT onboarding pack.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Seoul metropolitan commercial leased-office market benchmark for 3-month deposit and first-month rent allocation.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Bonded warehouse and liquor wholesale license preliminary application and customs bond preparation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: National Tax Service / Korea Customs Service
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No statutory license fee for liquor wholesale registration; bonded warehouse approval is conditionally granted without official fee, with compliance-consulting fees billed separately.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Bank service charge for issuing a reference letter and notarization/apostille support; may vary by bank tariff.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, Book IV (Companies), Articles 287-1 through 287-35 (Yuhan Hoesa / Limited Liability Company), especially Articles 287-5, 287-14, 287-21 and 287-25; Article 190 (existence upon registration); Local Tax Act for registration tax; Foreign Exchange Transactions Act for inward capital remittances; Liquor Tax Act and Customs Act for licensed operations.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: District Court Registration Office having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office, operated under the Korean Supreme Court Registration System (i-REG).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Articles of Incorporation and the Corporate Registration Application; the resulting legal instrument is the Certificate of Corporate Registration issued by the Court Registration Office.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. Korean law prescribes no statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Yuhan Hoesa. The subscribed capital stated in the Articles of Incorporation must be fully paid before registration, with the deposit placed in a bank escrow or blocked capital account at a licensed Korean bank. The bank's deposit certificate must be attached to the court registration filing. If the LLC is not registered, the deposit arrangement is void. For non-resident investors, inward remittance must be reported to the receiving bank under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and, if applicable, under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTION NO. 1 OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE MANAGERS AND DIRECTORS OF YUHAN HOESA, A LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY INCORPORATED UNDER THE COMMERCIAL ACT OF THE REPUBLIC OF KOREA.
WHEREAS the Company has been formed to carry on the business of bonded warehouse wholesale trade of aged Scotch whisky and Bordeaux wines; and WHEREAS the organizers and initial officers must perfect the corporate governance by adopting the registered office, subscribing and paying share capital, authorizing banking arrangements, appointing statutory officers, and delegating the necessary permitting authority.
NOW, BE IT RESOLVED, by the unanimous written consent of the initial directors and members, as follows:
1. Share Capital Subscription. The share capital set forth in the notarized Articles of Incorporation is hereby subscribed in full by the founding members. Each subscription is accepted on the condition that the amount payable is deposited, prior to court registration, in an escrow account with a bank licensed in Korea. Shares shall be issued, and ledger entries made, only when the bank's certificate of deposit is delivered to the registry. No share may be fractionally issued or pledged as collateral unless permitted by law.
2. Adoption of Registered Office. The registered office at the address designated in the Articles of Incorporation is hereby adopted. The Managing Director is authorized to sign the lease, to complete all post-registration notifications, and to ensure that the office sign and business registration reflect the registered address.
3. Banking and Treasury Authorization. The Managing Director is authorized to open deposit and securities accounts at a Korean bank, to execute the bank resolution, to issue wire transfer, SWIFT, and bonded transfer instructions, and to establish United States dollar and Korean won accounts for the purchase of bonded wines and spirits under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act.
4. Statutory Officer Appointments. The following statutorily required officers are appointed: [Full Name], Managing Director; [Full Name], Auditor; and [Full Name], Director of Compliance and Industrial Licensing. The Managing Director shall have general day-to-day managerial authority, the Auditor shall exercise the statutory audit and inspection powers, and the Compliance Director shall be responsible for all filings with the National Tax Service, Korea Customs Service, Ministry of Environment, and fire safety authorities.
5. Delegation and Ratification. The officers are authorized to engage Korean legal counsel, customs brokers and engineers; to execute license applications, environmental registrations and bond instruments; and to pay all formation expenses. All acts performed by the organizers prior to this resolution for the purpose of incorporation are hereby approved and ratified as though they were acts of the Company.
This resolution is binding on the Company, its members, and all successor officers, and remains effective until rescinded by a unanimous member and director resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Clearance and Preparation of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean Supreme Court Registration System (i-REG) and the District Court Registration Office with jurisdiction over the intended registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before filing, all founding members must complete a corporate name search against the registry database. The name of a Yuhan Hoesa must include the Korean suffix corresponding to Yuhan Hoesa and must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered company or to a trademark used by another liquor trader. Through the Supreme Court online registration portal, the organizers must clear the preferred name and then draft the Articles of Incorporation in Korean, with an optional English translation. Since the Company will operate bonded wine and spirits trade, the business-object clause must expressly state that the Company is authorized to conduct the wholesale distribution of alcoholic beverages, bonded warehouse warehousing, import and export, incidental customs brokerage, and any other business expressly permitted by the Commercial Act.
required_dossiers: Reserved corporate name confirmation certificate
Draft Articles of Incorporation
Identity documents (passport or national ID) of founding members
Corporate name search report
Statement of business purpose and intended licenses
Power of attorney if represented by a professional formation agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry rejects the name as confusingly similar, add a distinctive element or geographic qualifier, amend the draft Articles by unanimous member consent, and resubmit within two business days. If a priority dispute arises, file a petition for review with the Supreme Court Registration System and provide evidence of earlier lawful use.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of the Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A Korean Notary Public appointed by the Ministry of Justice, acting in the district where the incorporators attend
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All founding members must appear before the Korean notary to execute the Articles of Incorporation. For a Yuhan Hoesa, the notarial certificate is a mandatory registration attachment; the notary must verify that the incorporation is not contrary to mandatory law, that the members have legal capacity, and that the paid-in capital has been deposited or placed in a statutory escrow account. The notary will issue a Korean-language notarial certificate, which becomes the authoritative document for registration. An English translation may be attached for internal governance but does not replace the Korean notarial record. If a founding member is an offshore investor, foreign exchange deposit evidence must be provided and any required Foreign Investment Promotion Act declaration must be secured prior to execution.
required_dossiers: Original executed Articles of Incorporation
Identity verification documents for all members
Bank certificate of paid-in capital escrow deposit
Foreign investment declaration or inward remittance certificate, if applicable
Written consent of initial members to officer terms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary refuses to execute the Articles due to a missing declaration or a substantive legal defect, cure the identified omission, obtain an initial member resolution ratifying the correction, and re-execute before the same or another notary. No operational loss accrues if the correction is made within five business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Court Registration of the Yuhan Hoesa
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: District Court Registration Office with territorial jurisdiction over the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within ten business days after notarization, file the incorporation registration application with the competent District Court Registration Office. The court will verify the notarized Articles, the capital deposit certificate, the officers' consents and the payment of registration tax and local education surcharge. Once satisfied, the court will enter the Yuhan Hoesa in the Commercial Register and issue the Certificate of Corporate Registration. Under the Commercial Act, the Company acquires legal personality from the moment of registration. The registered office must be a physical Korean address; a post office box is not acceptable. After registration, the organizers must file a completed business registration with the local tax office within the statutory period.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Bank certificate proving paid-in capital deposit
Written consents of the Managing Director, Auditor and Compliance Director
Identity documents of all statutory officers
Prescribed court registration application form
Receipt of payment for registration tax and local education surcharge
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the court issues a correction order, rectify the indicated items within fourteen days and re-submit. If registration is rejected, file a motion for reconsideration with the same court chamber or re-apply after supplementary notarization. No business operations may commence until the Certificate of Corporate Registration is issued.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration and License Initiation with National Tax Service and Korea Customs Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service District Tax Office having jurisdiction over the registered office, and the Korea Customs Service District Customs Office for bonded trade authorizations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After court registration, management must file the corporate business registration application with the National Tax Service district tax office. In parallel, submit the liquor wholesale license application under the Liquor Tax Act and the bonded warehouse operator permit application under the Customs Act. The liquor wholesale license requires evidence of a licensed business place, criminal record certificates of the managing officers, and confirmation that no Korean national tax is delinquent. The bonded warehouse permit requires a warehouse layout, inventory control program, customs bond guarantee, and storage security plan. Customs and tax authorities may conduct a physical premises inspection before issuing the final licenses.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Corporate Registration
Business registration application form prescribed by the National Tax Service
Liquor wholesale license application under the Liquor Tax Act
Bonded warehouse operator permit application under the Customs Act
Lease or title evidence for the sales office and bonded warehouse
Criminal record certificates of directors and managing officers
Tax clearance certificate confirming no delinquent national taxes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the National Tax Service or Korea Customs Service issues a preliminary deficiency notice, submit a written supplementary response within ten business days. If a license application is denied, file an administrative appeal with the head of the relevant agency and, if necessary, with the Tax Tribunal or an administrative court for judicial review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Physical Industrial Licensing, Environmental Registration and Civil Defense Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korea Customs Service; National Tax Service; Ministry of Environment; local municipal government building and fire safety departments; Ministry of Employment and Labor for occupational safety
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the business license is issued, complete the physical licensing package. For any newly constructed or altered warehouse, obtain municipal building use approval and fire safety design review before operation. Submit an environmental registration or small-scale environmental impact assessment to the Ministry of Environment if the project falls within the statutory screening categories. Obtain the bonded warehouse operator permit from Korea Customs Service only after physical inspection confirms secure storage, goods segregation, inventory record integrity, and fire protection. The Ministry of Employment and Labor must receive an occupational safety risk assessment and workplace opening report. All licenses are integrated into the Company's compliance calendar before the first customs bonded transfer is executed.
required_dossiers: Bonded warehouse operator permit application
Liquor wholesale license approval record
Building use permit and structural safety certificate
Fire safety certificate and emergency evacuation plan
Environmental registration or EIA screening submission
Occupational safety risk assessment
Customs bond guarantee or security deposit
Warehouse layout and bonded inventory control program
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any industrial license is queried, cure the noted defect and file an amended application within the official response period. If the environmental authority requires a higher EIA tier, commission an environmental consultant and submit a supplementary impact assessment. Rejection by Korea Customs Service may be challenged by an administrative appeal to the Commissioner of Korea Customs, followed by a district administrative court proceeding.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Korea Customs Service (Bonded Facilities Division) and the relevant District Customs Office; National Tax Service District Tax Office (Liquor Tax Section); Ministry of Environment and local environmental authority; local municipal government for building and fire safety; Ministry of Employment and Labor for occupational safety.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Liquor Wholesale Business License under the Liquor Tax Act and Bonded Warehouse Operator Permit under the Customs Act; additional Fire Protection System Certificate, Building Use Permit and Occupational Safety and Health Act workplace clearance.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment (MOE), together with the Korea Environment Corporation and the applicable local environmental protection authority
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 3 / Environmental Registration. A full Environmental Impact Assessment Report or Small-Scale Environmental Impact Assessment is required only if the project falls within the statutory project types in the Environmental Impact Assessment Act, such as an industrial complex, large logistics facility, or a warehouse whose total floor area exceeds the screening threshold, or where construction occurs on sensitive land. A bonded warehouse used solely for storage and wholesale transfer of wine and spirits is ordinarily exempt from a full EIA subject to environmental registration and compliance with local land use conditions.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater or process VOC emissions are generated by bonded wine and spirit storage. Sanitary and storm wastewater must comply with the Water Environment Conservation Act final effluent standards, including BOD not exceeding 30 mg/L, TSS not exceeding 40 mg/L, COD not exceeding 40 mg/L, T-N not exceeding 60 mg/L and T-P not exceeding 8 mg/L, unless a stricter local effluent limitation applies. Refrigerant systems, if used, must not use chlorofluorocarbons or other controlled substances under the Ozone Layer Protection Act. If aggregate VOC release from spilled alcohol or barrel aging exceeds the reporting threshold under the Clean Air Conservation Act, the Company must install vapor recovery equipment and submit periodic emission reports. Contaminated absorbents, broken wine cases and hazardous cleaning wastes must be stored separately, manifested, and transferred only to licensed waste treatment operators under the Waste Management Act.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate issued by the competent fire department after inspection of extinguishing systems, exit routes, emergency lighting and sprinkler systems; required when total floor area exceeds the Fire Act thresholds. A structural load inspection certificate and building use approval must be obtained from the local government, with particular attention to high rack storage and seismic loads. Occupancy and operation require an occupational safety clearance under the Occupational Safety and Health Act, including a workplace risk assessment, hazard communication for alcohol vapors and manual handling risks, worker safety training, evacuation drills, and a fire prevention plan coordinated with the local civil defense authority.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea, operating through the HomeTax electronic portal (www.hometax.go.kr); Korea Customs Service (UNI-PASS) is the competent authority for export clearance and bonded-warehouse supervision.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign non-resident entity establishing a Korean Yuhan Hoesa LLC: (1) register the company with the competent Korean court registry to obtain the corporate registration number; (2) file the statutory Application for Business Registration with the district tax office having jurisdiction over the domestic place of business within 20 days from the commencement of business in Korea; (3) attach the company articles of incorporation, corporate seal certificate, domestic place-of-business lease agreement, proof of registered capital, and notarized/apostilled documents of the overseas parent company, together with a power of attorney designating a Korean tax representative where required; (4) obtain the Business Registration Certificate containing the 10-digit Business Registration Number, which is the unified Tax Identification Number (TIN) and VAT registration number; (5) enrol in HomeTax using an accredited digital certificate, file the initial zero turnover VAT return if no supplies have been made, and maintain subordinate registrations for bonded-warehouse licences with Korea Customs Service.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Korea provides no check-the-box or elective entity classification regime. Hybrid mismatch rules are applied through the Adjustment of International Taxes Act, but no statutory election is available to reclassify a Yuhan Hoesa LLC for Korean tax purposes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Value-Added Tax) under the Value-Added Tax Act of the Republic of Korea
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No Korean Won threshold for corporate entities: a domestic Yuhan Hoesa LLC is required to register for VAT/Business Operator Registration immediately upon commencement of business, irrespective of turnover. Unincorporated small operators have simplified taxpayer statuses, but these do not apply to a corporation.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All VAT-registered businesses, including the Yuhan Hoesa LLC, must issue electronic tax invoices via the NTS HomeTax system. Each B2B electronic tax invoice must be transmitted to the NTS within the day immediately following the supply date. No physical stamping or pre-clearance approval is required; the NTS performs real-time data clearance using the national e-Tax Invoice network and cross-matches invoice data with Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS records for bonded trade. Accredited digital certificates are mandatory, and third-party service providers may use NTS-certified transmission channels. Failure to issue, late issuance, or false issuance of e-Tax Invoices triggers additional tax and digital anti-fraud penalties under the Value-Added Tax Act.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For goods, 0% VAT applies when goods are exported from Korea to a foreign purchaser; a valid Korea Customs Service electronic export declaration must evidence the actual departure, and in bonded-warehouse wholesale trade, the wines/spirits must move from the bonded warehouse to export under customs supervision. The title, risk, and economic ownership must pass to the non-resident counterparty, and the export sale must be supported by the foreign-exchange receipt within the prescribed deadline. For qualifying offshore digital services, zero-rating requires that the service is supplied to, and received by, a person outside Korea and consumed entirely outside Korea; the supplier must retain contracts, work orders, and usage logs. Mere shipment to an overseas intermediary without actual export, or goods diverted into domestic consumption, cannot be zero-rated.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service electronic Export Declaration (UNI-PASS export clearance record)
Original Bill of Lading (or air waybill) evidencing physical shipment from Korea
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or Foreign Exchange Receipt Certificate issued by a licensed Korean foreign exchange bank under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
Commercial invoice and packing list corresponding to the export declaration
Bonded warehouse customs transfer/export approval record (for wines/spirits under bonded trade licence)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Zero-rated export claims are automatically cross-checked by the NTS against Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS departure records and foreign exchange bank reporting. If any mandatory document is missing or inconsistent, the 0% rate is reversed and VAT is assessed at 10% on the total export consideration, plus the additional tax penalties and interest prescribed by the Framework Act on National Taxes and the Value-Added Tax Act. False export invoices, circular transactions, or fraudulent export declarations constitute tax evasion and may result in criminal sanctions and imprisonment under the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act, revocation of bonded-warehouse licences, and retrospective clawback of all VAT refunds previously claimed on the zero-rated transactions for the statutory limitation period. Non-receipt of foreign exchange within the deadline without an approved extension can also invalidate the zero-rating and trigger fines under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) is the central bank and custodian of foreign-exchange settlement statistics, while the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) retains policy authority under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act; the Korea Customs Service (KCS) separately supervises cross-border trade declarations and bonded warehouse controls.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea is an OECD member with a substantially liberalized, yet still documentation-heavy, foreign-exchange regime. The Korean won (KRW) is fully convertible on the onshore interbank market but is not freely deliverable offshore. Current-account transactions, including trade settlement for bonded wine and spirits, service fees, royalties, and salaries, are generally permissible without quantitative ceilings, provided the authorized foreign-exchange bank receives the underlying contract, invoice, transport documents, and customs declaration. Capital-account transactions such as foreign direct investment, equity injections, intercompany loans, and profit remittances require a report or prior declaration under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. In practice, repatriation of dividends is achievable after corporate tax and withholding tax requirements are met, but the treasury must demonstrate that the profits are real, audited, and properly distributed. Export proceeds must be repatriated into Korea within the statutory time frame and either credited to a licensed foreign-currency account or converted into KRW. The Korean tax and customs authority examines bonded wine and spirits flows through the UNI-PASS system, meaning global treasury transfers must align precisely with customs invoices, LC documentation, and KCS bonded warehouse records. There are no current-account quotas, but the KRW serves as a managed float, and the compliance cost is primarily procedural: purpose codes, underlying exposure, entity verification, and post-event reporting to the Bank of Korea and MOEF.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, export proceeds must be collected and repatriated to an authorized foreign-exchange bank in Korea within 18 months from the date of export declaration. There is no fixed statutory percentage surrender ratio into KRW; the exporter may retain the foreign currency in a designated foreign-currency account or voluntarily convert it to KRW at the onshore market rate. However, 100% of the export proceeds must physically return to a Korean authorized bank account within the 18-month window unless prior advance approval is obtained from the MOEF or Bank of Korea for exceptional deferment. For bonded warehouse trade, the same repatriation obligation applies, and any retention of export proceeds abroad without proper reporting is treated as an unresolved foreign-exchange violation.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Bonded Warehouse Customs Duty and VAT Payment Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low and legally non-viable for this treasury blueprint. Offshore digital EMI platforms are not licensed as authorized foreign-exchange banks under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and cannot perform the mandatory reporting to the Bank of Korea, MOEF, or Korea Customs Service for bonded import settlements, capital injections, or VAT/duty payments. The alternate payment service provider license under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act is limited to domestic payment facilitation, not cross-border corporate treasury or bonded warehouse clearing. Therefore, all inbound equity, trade settlement, and outbound payment flows must route through a Korean commercial bank or a licensed foreign-exchange bank branch with physical presence in Korea. EMIs may be used only as a supplementary information layer, never as a legal account-holding treasury rail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a foreign-controlled Yuhan Hoesa engaged in high-risk bonded trade, Korean banks generally mandate at least one statutory director or authorized signatory to appear physically at the branch for an in-person KYC interview with the original passport, corporate registry certificate, business license, corporate seal certificate, tax registration certificate, and a substantive office address proof. Remote consular proxy opening is not accepted by Tier-1 Korean banks for this sector. A notarized and apostilled power of attorney may allow a local certified accountant to assist with document submission and account administration, but the initial underwriting interview and biometric verification still require an in-person director visit. The bank compliance committee typically insists on direct identification of signatories because of the money-laundering risk present in premium wine and spirits trading.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-value premium spirits with opaque vintage valuation and limited price discovery, exposing trade-based money-laundering risk through over or under-invoicing.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The entity must provide independent market valuation reports from recognized auction houses or indices such as Liv-ex, signed commercial invoices from the distillery or négociant showing exact bottle age and bottle count, the relevant Incoterms, original bills of lading, full LLoyd’s marine and transit insurance certificates, certified warehouse custody receipts, and KCS conversation reports that reconcile the customs value with the LC value.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex beneficial ownership structure involving a foreign parent, nominee shareholders, and a Korean statutory director who has no revenue or operating history.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The compliance file must include current Korea FIU beneficial ownership declarations, organizational chart from top parent to the Korean Yuhan Hoesa, audited financial statements of all shareholders, no-nominee declarations signed by the ultimate beneficial owner, banker’s reference letters from the parent company’s bank, proof of source of wealth, and documentary evidence that the statutory Korean director is operationally active, including employment contracts, lease agreements, utility bills in the company’s name, and social insurance filings.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Bonded warehouse cross-border flows from Scotland and Bordeaux via intermediaries in low-tax or transit jurisdictions, creating uncertainty as to whether funds correspond to physical goods moving under Korean customs bond.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The treasury must provide the full purchase sale and logistics chain: original contract between the Korean entity and the ultimate EU supplier, intermediate broker agreements, customs-approved bonded warehouse transfer forms, KCS UNI-PASS import declarations, bonded entry and withdrawal records, real warehouse inventory reconciliation at month-end, export or import trade settlement statements from the Korean authorized bank, and the corresponding SWIFT MT103 or LC payment references.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Suspicious inbound capital injection from a jurisdiction not aligned with the stated shareholder profile, or money flowing into a capital escrow account without an underlying foreign-investment declaration.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The entity must submit a pre-investment FDI report acknowledgement from the authorized Korean bank or MOEF, the Foreign Investment Registration Certificate, board resolution approving the capital increase, notarized passport of the remitting shareholder, bank statement from the remitting account showing legitimate accumulated earnings, a certified source-of-wealth declaration, and a detailed business plan proving that the injected capital will be used for bonded warehouse operations, duty payments, and initial inventory purchases.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound capital must first be declared through a designated authorized foreign-exchange bank in Korea under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. The foreign shareholder should remit via SWIFT MT103 with an investment remittance purpose code and the FDI report number in the reference field. The Korean bank will credit the funds to the company’s capital escrow account in KRW or an approved foreign currency account; if received in a foreign currency, the company may convert to KRW at the onshore market rate. After the deposit is verified, a certified public accountant issues a capital contribution verification report used to update the company registry. Profit distributions follow a separate route: audited financial statements, tax clearance, dividend withholding tax settlement, and a corporate resolution of the Yuhan Hoesa must be presented to the bank so that the dividend can be converted and remitted abroad through the SWIFT platform with a valid royalty or dividend settlement purpose code.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For imports of aged Scotch and Bordeaux, the primary clearing rail is the irrevocable documentary letter of credit opened by the Korean bank in favor of the foreign supplier, using SWIFT MT700 to issue the LC, MT799 for amendments, and MT103 for final reimbursement at maturity. For lower-risk repeat transactions, direct SWIFT MT103 wire payments against pro-forma invoices and scanned shipping documents may be used. Documentary collections on D/P and D/A terms are acceptable for established counterparties, with the presenting bank instructed to release documents only against payment or acceptance. All customs duty and VAT liabilities associated with bonded warehouse operations must be settled through the Korean bank’s virtual account integrated with the Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS system. Transfers between bonded warehouses, known as bonded transfers, must be reported through the KCS electronic system and supported by warehouse custody receipts, with no separate external SWIFT clearing required for the tax-suspended movement of goods.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable onshore KRW/USD outright forwards and foreign exchange swaps through an authorized Korean bank, permitted only when the company holds a verified trade exposure toward the wine/spirits supplier or buyer

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) booked in the Seoul interbank market, permitted strictly for hedging the unremitted dividend or trade receivable exposure and prohibited for speculative or naked positions
Cross-currency swaps between KRW and EUR or GBP for long-term financing of bonded warehouse inventory and vintage purchase facilities, limited to hedging actual principal and interest obligations

Foreign exchange options for purchase of wine inventory priced in EUR and GBP, eligible when the notional amount does not exceed the underlying customs-verified transaction value and when the bank receives the supplier contract and KCS import declaration as supporting evidence

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return, tax-adjusted financial statements and, if triggered, independent CPA audit report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) district tax office; Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) for externally audited filings
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 March of the year following a 31 December fiscal year-end; 60-day extension available under the Corporate Tax Act with a potential additional 60-day extension for overseas audited branches; audited financial statements must accompany the NTS return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing incurs a 20% unfaithful-return surtax on unpaid corporate tax plus 0.03% daily late-payment interest; understatement surtax can reach 30%; five consecutive years of non-filing may trigger administrative strike-off of the NTS business registration and referral for criminal tax evasion.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local corporate income tax return and payment (Si-Gun-Gu surtax on corporate income)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local government (Si/Gun/Gu) through the National Tax Service single corporate-tax filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same statutory date as the national corporate tax filing: 31 March following the fiscal year-end; no independent extension unless the NTS extension is granted
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or deficient local corporate income tax attracts local tax surtax of up to 40% of the assessed amount plus 0.03% daily interest; continued non-payment permits municipal tax attachment, enforcement and administrative cancellation of the business licence.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-Added Tax returns, including preliminary returns for high-turnover taxpayers and final semi-annual returns
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service district tax office of the registered head office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a corporation with prior-year taxable supplies of at least KRW 80,000,000: preliminary VAT returns for January-March, April-June and July-September due by 25 April, 25 July and 25 October, and a final October-December return due by 25 January; for all other VAT taxpayers: semi-annual returns for January-June and July-December due by 25 July and 25 January
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: VAT late-filing surtax of 10% to 20% of unpaid tax, plus 0.03% daily late-payment interest; repeated failure to file may produce NTS business-registration strike-off and disqualification from the liquor wholesaling licence.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Liquor tax return and bonded warehouse release reconciliation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service regional tax office issuing the liquor licence; Korea Customs Service for bonded warehouse custody and release controls
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly return by the last day of the month following the month in which wine or spirits are released from bonded storage for domestic wholesale consumption; annual bonded inventory reconciliation and licence-condition report due by 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: False or late liquor-tax returns attract a 20% unfaithful-return penalty plus 0.03% daily interest; mismatched bonded records can suspend or revoke the liquor wholesaling licence and bonded warehouse approval and cause immediate acceleration of the full liquor tax, education tax and customs duty.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory external audit report under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service external audit disclosure system; NTS tax file; competent District Court registration office only where court-filed audited financial statements are prescribed
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Audit report must be submitted to the annual members' meeting and delivered to FSS where applicable within two weeks after that meeting; in all events it must accompany the corporate tax return by 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint a registered CPA auditor or to file the audit report may impose administrative fines and criminal penalties on directors, suspension of the liquor licence, administrative strike-off of the business registration and rejection of the corporate tax return as incomplete.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual members' general meeting approval of financial statements and maintenance of statutory minutes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company registered office; competent District Court registration office only where the meeting resolution alters capital, articles or quota ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual members' meeting must be held no later than the corporate tax filing deadline of 31 March for a 31 December fiscal year-end; minutes signed and retained at the registered office; court registration of any registrable resolution within 30 days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to hold or minute the annual meeting is a Commercial Act violation punishable by fines; unregistered quota transfers become ineffective against third parties and may destroy limited-liability protection in abusive cases.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual liquor wholesaling and bonded warehouse operator licence-condition report and sales/inventory certification
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service regional tax office and Korea Customs Service
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 March for the preceding calendar year; quarterly sales/inventory report dates continue to apply under the licence where the licence so prescribes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or falsification can trigger immediate suspension and administrative strike-off of the liquor wholesaling licence and bonded warehouse authorization, forfeiture or restriction of bonded-transfer privileges, administrative fines and prohibition on further wine/spirits bonded trade.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Korean Act on External Audit of Stock Companies and its Enforcement Decree, an independent registered-certified-PA audit is mandatory if any of the following quantitative criteria is met as of the immediately preceding fiscal year-end: (i) the company is a listed company or a financial institution; (ii) total assets equal or exceed KRW 12,000,000,000 (approximately USD 9.1 million); (iii) annual revenue equals or exceeds KRW 70,000,000,000 (approximately USD 53 million); (iv) the company has 300 or more employees and therefore no longer qualifies for the SME audit exemption; or (v) the National Tax Service or Korea Customs Service imposes audited financial statements as a licensing condition for the liquor wholesaling or bonded warehouse operation. The audit must be performed by a Korean registered CPA and the report must be presented to the annual members' meeting and filed with the Financial Supervisory Service where required.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) for listed and financial entities; Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (K-GAAP) for the private Yuhan Hoesa LLC; audits are conducted under Korean Standards on Auditing (KSA); bonded wine and spirits inventories must also satisfy the Customs Valuation Act and inventory-valuation requirements equivalent to IAS 2 where an audit is triggered.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Korea does not maintain a public annual UBO filing for a private LLC. The statutory protocol is as follows: (a) maintain a physically current quota-member register at the registered office; (b) within 30 days of any quota transfer approved by the members' general meeting, complete court registration at the competent District Court and update the member register and the AML/client-due-diligence file; (c) report any change in the representative or a 10% or greater quota holder to the National Tax Service within 30 days so the corporate tax and electronic tax-invoice registration remains accurate; and (d) at each annual members' meeting certify to the auditor, where appointed, that the beneficial-ownership schedule in the accounting records matches the quotaholders of record. Failure to update within the 30-day window makes the transfer ineffective against third parties and exposes controllers to Korean AML penalties and possible piercing of limited liability in tax-evasion cases.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (quota holders and cyanu holders)
Register of Directors and non-executive officers where appointed
Register of Charges, mortgages and security interests
Minutes of Members' General Meetings and Director Meetings
Accounting books, vouchers and supporting customs/liquor-tax records

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 400 to USD 1,500 per annum for a professional registered office and company secretarial agent in Seoul, excluding commercial rent and legal representation; USD 1,200 to USD 3,500 per annum where NTS representation and annual filing handling are included
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 to USD 8,000 for a small or medium non-listed LLC with clean records; USD 10,000 to USD 25,000 for a bonded wine/spirits wholesale operation

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 21% national Corporate Income Tax top bracket for taxable income exceeding KRW 20 billion; the combined top effective rate is 23.1% after adding the 10% Local Income Tax surcharge (national rate brackets: 9% up to KRW 200 million; 19% from KRW 200 million to KRW 20 billion; 21% above KRW 20 billion).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: South Korea does not provide a general patent box or CIT holiday for bonded wine-spirits wholesale trade. Limited R&D tax credits (up to 25% of qualifying R&D expenditure under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act), job-creation tax credits, and free-zone foreign investment tax incentives under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act may apply only to qualifying high-technology FDI, which an ordinary Yuhan Hoesa engaged in ISIC 4632 bonded wine wholesale would normally not meet. Bonded warehouse status defers customs duties and individual consumption tax; it does not reduce corporate income tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: NTS HomeTax electronic filing portal (hometax.go.kr), Form: 'Corporate Tax Standard Return and Self-Assessment' (Corporate Tax Basis and Tax Computation Statement; Form 41-4, together with the local income tax integrated filing schedule).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual final return; inter-year semi-annual corporate tax prepayment due by 31 August for calendar-year taxpayers; monthly withholding tax and VAT returns filed separately.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual corporate tax return must be filed within 3 months after the end of the fiscal year. For a calendar-year Yuhan Hoesa, the normal deadline is 31 March; an additional one-month extension is available when financial statements are examined and certified by an external tax accountant or independent auditor, making the extended deadline 30 April.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declare total gross revenue from the bonded warehouse wholesale trade of aged scotch whiskies and Bordeaux wines, including duty-paid sales proceeds, bonded transfer fees, commissions, and handling charges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All cross-border sales revenue must be converted to KRW at the transaction-date exchange rate or a lawful proxy rate. Revenue from a non-resident affiliate cannot be netted against cost of goods, warehouse rental, or customer incentives. Every delayed remittance receivable must be tracked; non-operating foreign exchange differences are reported in Box 6.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduct direct costs: bonded goods purchases, customs duties, liquor/individual consumption tax actually paid upon withdrawal from the bonded warehouse, ocean freight, inland freight, insurance, and inbound inspection fees attributable to products sold.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductions are allowed only for costs incurred in performing transactions with unrelated parties at arm's length or with related parties supported by contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation. Purchases from a French or Scottish related supplying entity must be evidenced by vendor invoices, B/L, and customs declarations. Unrealistically inflated transfer prices are reportable and adjustable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross profit is computed as Box 1 minus Box 2.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a Korean wholesale distributor of luxury alcoholic beverages, gross margin must be benchmarked against independent distributors. If the margin falls outside the interquartile range of comparables, the NTS may apply a transfer pricing adjustment unless a correct transactional profit or resale price analysis is attached.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 - Selling, General and Administrative Expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Include rent for the bonded warehouse, utilities, salaries, insurance, telecommunication, legal and accounting fees, promotional expenses, and royalties for trademarks and distribution rights.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payments to a foreign affiliate for management fees, IT services, insurance, or marketing support are deductible only if the service was actually rendered, confers a real commercial benefit, and is priced at arm's length. If a foreign affiliate is a shell entity without staff or substance, the expense must be added back. Korean-sourced service fees paid to non-residents are also subject to withholding tax under Korean domestic law.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Derived as gross profit minus SG&A expenses, before non-operating items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: An artificial recurring loss while foreign shareholders receive commissions is a classic red flag. If ordinary loss arises from related-party wine purchasing, the taxpayer must supply a detailed transfer pricing study. Losses cannot be remitted to a foreign head office, and a non-resident shareholder cannot claim group relief through the Korean entity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Include interest income, dividend income, foreign exchange gains and losses on SWIFT wire remittances and bonded-transfer receivables, donation expenses, and provision reversals.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest and royalty payments made to non-residents must be separately stated, matched with withholding tax returns, and supported by Tax Residency Certificate and beneficial ownership evidence. Foreign-currency indebtedness from non-resident controlling shareholders must be tested under the Korean thin capitalization rule; the deductible debt-to-equity ratio is 2:1 for most corporations, and disallowed interest is added back on a separate adjustment schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 - Tax Adjustments / Add-backs and Deductible Reserves
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconcile accounting net income to taxable income by adding disallowed expenses (entertainment exceeding statutory limits, penalties, bribes, non-qualifying reserves) and deducting non-taxable income and permitted tax-specific reserves.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border payments are heavily scrutinized at this stage. Royalties paid to non-resident shareholders for trademark use must satisfy beneficial ownership and royalty-rate reasonableness; if no actual trademark is exploited in Korea, the deduction is fully denied and may be recharacterized as a dividend distribution subject to 22% withholding. Any entertainment expense related to foreign customers must meet documentary requirements to avoid 100% add-back.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Subtract net operating losses carried forward from previous fiscal years, up to 15 years, where the statutory requirements for continuation of the same business and shareholder continuity are met.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses must be computed under the Korean Corporate Tax Act, not IFRS or foreign GAAP. If a foreign investor acquires more than 50% of the shares and the main business is not maintained, loss carryforward may be denied. The loss schedule should identify each originating fiscal year and audited financial statements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total taxable income after prior-year loss deduction is entered before applying progressive tax rates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Korean domestic Yuhan Hoesa is taxed on its worldwide income. Foreign-source income items must be included here unless exempted by a treaty; if foreign tax was withheld on overseas sales commissions, foreign tax credit is claimed later in Box 11, not by excluding income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply progressive Corporate Income Tax rates of 9%, 19% and 21% to the taxable income brackets, then compute the 10% Local Income Tax surcharge.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders have no direct effect on the entity-level tax computation. Profits are taxed at the Yuhan Hoesa level; subsequent dividend distributions to non-residents are not deductible and are separately subject to withholding tax. The box should reflect the exact geometric calculation including the local surcharge.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 11 - Tax Credits and Foreign Tax Credit
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim domestic tax credits such as R&D credits, foreign tax credits, and tax credit for dividends received from foreign subsidiaries after satisfying minimum holding and substantiation requirements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits may be claimed on Korean-source taxes paid to a foreign jurisdiction on income also taxed in Korea, subject to per-country or overall limits. The foreign tax credit amount must be supported by official foreign tax assessment or withholding certificates. A non-resident director cannot personally claim this credit in the corporation's return.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file by the statutory deadline triggers an unfaithful return additional tax of 20% of the unpaid tax, or 40% when the omission is fraudulent or grossly negligent. Underreported taxable income without fraud triggers a 10% understatement penalty; fraudulent understatement triggers 40%. Late payment interest accrues monthly on unpaid amounts, and the NTS may impose a 30% additional tax on unfaithful withholding by a resident withholding agent. Repeated non-filing or the omission of transaction amounts exceeding prescribed thresholds exposes the company to compulsory tax collection, seizure of bonded inventory, and criminal referral under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act. In egregious cases, the NTS publicly discloses the taxpayer's identity after 2 years of delinquent tax above KRW 500 million, names the director as a serious tax defaulter, and imposes a travel ban (immigration blacklisting).

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% on outbound dividends paid by a Korean Yuhan Hoesa to a non-resident shareholder, composed of 20% national withholding tax plus 2% Local Income Tax surcharge, unless reduced under an applicable double tax treaty (DTA), typically to 5%, 10%, or 15% depending on the treaty, the shareholding threshold, and the recipient's beneficial ownership and holding period.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim reduced DTA withholding on dividends, interest, or royalties, the non-resident recipient must deliver to the Korean withholding agent before payment: (i) a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the tax authority of the treaty jurisdiction for the relevant tax year; (ii) a Beneficial Ownership Statement certifying that the recipient is the actual owner and not a conduit for another jurisdiction; (iii) proof of shareholding in and any required minimum holding period of the Korean Yuhan Hoesa; and (iv) any specific treaty claim form required by the National Tax Service. The Korean paying company files a reduced withholding application with the NTS District Director or, if treaty relief is denied, pays the statutory 22% and the recipient files a refund claim within the statutory limitation period. The NTS will deny the treaty claim if the foreign entity lacks economic substance to hold assets, make decisions, or bear risk in the residence state, and will recharacterize the income and impose penalties under Korea's International Tax Coordination Act General Anti-Abuse Rule.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Korean withholding is 22% (20% national plus 2% local) for outbound interest and royalties. Under many Korean DTAs the treaty rates are 0% to 15% for interest and 5% to 15% for royalties, depending on the treaty and the recipient's beneficial ownership. For royalties paid for trademarks, copyrights, or industrial know-how used in Korea, the Korean payer must withhold at the statutory rate unless a fully documented treaty claim is in place; a mere intercompany invoice without evidence that the intellectual property is actually exploited in Korea is treated as a constructive dividend and loses treaty protection.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 10 billion in aggregate annual foreign related-party transactions triggers the mandatory Local File; KRW 50 billion triggers the Master File; consolidated group revenue of KRW 1 trillion triggers the Country-by-Country Report. The threshold is measured by the value of intercompany purchases, sales, loans, royalties, and service fees during the fiscal year.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Korea does not maintain a standalone Economic Substance Regulations code, but the corporate veil and treaty benefit claims are scrutinized under the substance-over-form doctrine, the OECD BEPS beneficial ownership standards, and Article 51 of the International Tax Coordination Act (GAAR). A Yuhan Hoesa engaged in bonded wine and spirits trade must demonstrate real Core Income-Generating Activities in Korea: contractual negotiation, purchase buying and inventory decision-making, bonded warehouse lease and license holding, physical custody and risk of loss for beverage inventory, staff payroll, board meetings, accounting records, and portfolio risk management. A business that performs only booking entries in Korea while foreign shareholders or affiliates manage the wine sourcing, marketing, pricing, and financing from outside Korea is vulnerable to being treated as a shell company; the NTS may deny treaty protection, disallow related-party deductions, and pierce the entity to hold the ultimate beneficial owner and directors personally liable.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Customs Duty Evasion and Illicit Bonded Diversion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Removing or selling bonded aged scotch whisky and Bordeaux wine into the Korean domestic market without paying customs duties and individual consumption tax, knowingly falsely declaring product origin, volume, alcohol strength, or tariff classification in UNI-PASS, or using the bonded warehouse as cover for smuggling and under-declared sales.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Violation of the Customs Act provisions against false declarations and unlawful removal from customs bonded areas; the NTS/Customs authorities assess customs duty, individual consumption tax, VAT, and a surcharge of up to 40% of the evaded amount. Criminal penalties under the Customs Act and the Act on the Aggravated Punishment of Specific Economic Crimes include imprisonment for up to 5 years and fines of up to 5 times the amount evaded. The bonded warehouse license is revoked, and import-export privileges are suspended.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who participate in, order, or knowingly benefit from the bonded diversion are joint and severally liable for the unpaid duties, additional taxes, and penalties. Civil seizure of personal assets, bank accounts, and residences is permitted. Directors are subject to criminal imprisonment up to 5 years and, where the evasion exceeds KRW 500 million, up to 10 years in aggravated cases. The NTS imposes immigration control blacklisting and a travel ban on the director and beneficial owner, and the company's name and the director's personal identity are published as a serious tax defaulter.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: International Profit Shifting / Transfer Pricing Offense
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying inflated storage fees, blending fees, or management fees to a non-resident affiliate in Hong Kong, Singapore, the U.K., or France without any supporting service activity; deliberately setting a transfer price for imported wine bottles outside the arm's length range; failing to prepare and submit the Local File, Master File, and all intercompany transaction disclosures while the Korean entity continues to produce losses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The NTS makes an arm's length transfer pricing adjustment under Articles 4 and 5 of the International Tax Coordination Act, increases the Korean taxable income, and imposes an additional tax of 10% for underreporting or 30% to 40% for fraudulent manipulation under the Framework Act on National Taxes and the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act. Criminal sanctions under Article 3 of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act include imprisonment for up to 2 years or a fine not exceeding 3 times the tax evaded; repeated or large-scale evasion involving more than KRW 500 million carries imprisonment of up to 5 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierced where the director signed a false corporate tax return or instructed the use of a sham intermediary; directors may be held personally liable for the additional tax, penalties, and interest via civil judgment under the Commercial Act. The NTS attaches personal bank accounts and overseas estate assets through tax collection procedures, imposes a travel ban and immigration blacklisting, and refers directors to prosecutors for criminal fraud. In aggravated restitution cases, the court orders personal assets forfeited or sold to satisfy the evaded corporate tax.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Entity and Abusive Treaty Shopping / Beneficial Ownership Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Structuring the Korean Yuhan Hoesa as a thin shell through which profits are paid out as deductible royalties, interest, or service fees to a letterbox entity located in a favorable treaty jurisdiction, while the ultimate beneficial owner resides in a third country; or placing nominee shareholders in a treaty country solely to obtain reduced withholding dividend rates on profits generated by activities actually conducted in Korea.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 51 of the International Tax Coordination Act empowers the NTS to disregard the abusive arrangement, deny the treaty benefit, and recharacterize the payments as taxable dividends, interest, or ordinary income. The company is assessed additional CORPORATE income tax, withholding tax at the statutory 22% rate, and punitive penalties up to 40% for fraudulent underreporting. The Foreign Exchange Transactions Act penalties for unauthorized capital outflows and false remittance declarations also apply, and the scheme is reported to the Financial Intelligence Unit as potential money laundering.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who executed nominee agreements, false beneficial ownership certificates, or abusive conduit invoices are treated as co-conspirators. Courts pierce the corporate veil and hold directors personally liable for restitution of all unpaid taxes, interest, and penalties to the NTS. Civil asset restitution reaches personal properties in Korea and abroad; travel bans, immigration blacklisting, and asset freezes are imposed on controlling directors. Criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act can yield imprisonment up to 10 years for aggravated evasion, with mandatory confiscation of personal assets acquired through the unlawful scheme.
